architectural_risks.description: Open, evidence-driven set. No fixed length -- do not pad or truncate to match a target count. Each item's finding_id must be unique within this array.

finding_id.description: GENERATED, not chosen from a fixed list. Format: {CATEGORY-SLUG}-{NN}, where CATEGORY-SLUG is derived from this finding's own risk_category (see mapping below) and NN is a two-digit sequence number starting at 01, unique within that category for this output. Example: if risk_category is 'Upgradeability', finding_id is 'UPGRADEABILITY-01' (or -02 if a second, independent Upgradeability finding exists in this run). NOT a stable cross-protocol key -- do not assume this ID means the same thing across two different protocol runs. NOT stable across repeated runs on the SAME protocol either -- use claim_id for that (see below).

risk_category.description: Exact human-readable enum value, WITH a space -- e.g. 'Asset Custody', 'Economic Dependency'. This is a different format from the hyphenated slug used inside finding_id (e.g. 'ASSET-CUSTODY-01') -- do not use the hyphenated slug here.

claim_id.description: STABLE identifier for the underlying architectural proposition this finding makes, independent of finding_id and risk_category (both of which are known to vary across repeated runs on identical input -- see reproducibility test results). Format: {PROTOCOL-SLUG}-{TOKEN}...(1-6 mechanism tokens after the protocol slug; a single-token claim is valid when the finding genuinely turns on one mechanism), built ONLY from literal function/variable/state-variable names that already appear verbatim in this finding's own evidence array, uppercased, sorted alphabetically, hyphen-joined. Underscores within a token (e.g. Solidity internal-function convention '_setImplementation') are preserved, not stripped. Never derived from risk_category, severity, risk_name, or any other judgment field -- those are exactly the fields that drift between runs. See CLAIM ID & VALIDATION TARGET for the full algorithm and a worked example.

validation_target.description: Structured target for downstream deterministic (Foundry) validation. Exists so validation can key against a stable proposition instead of this run's finding_id/risk_category placement.

protocol.description: Protocol name/slug as given in this run's input (e.g. 'Venus', 'Aave').

primary_component.description: Single contract/module name most directly responsible for this claim, copied verbatim from the Architecture Model's contract_profile.name or affected_components -- not paraphrased.

mechanism_tokens.description: The literal function/variable/state names claim_id was built from, copied verbatim from this finding's evidence. Same tokens used to build claim_id, listed here as a structured array (not uppercased/hyphenated -- keep original casing as it appears in source, e.g. 'exchangeRateStoredInternal', not 'EXCHANGERATESTOREDINTERNAL').

dependency_chain.description: Ordered causal chain of function/state names from the outermost policy-facing call to the root data source, e.g. ['exchangeRateStoredInternal', 'getCashPrior', 'balanceOf']. Empty array if this claim has no meaningful multi-step chain (e.g. a single-hop privilege finding).

governance_model.description: ONE value for this finding's single most central privileged entity -- never an object, never per-entity. If multiple entities are involved, classify only the one most directly responsible for the exposure and describe the others in evidence/description text instead.

related_risks.description: finding_id values of related findings from THIS SAME output only.

mitigation_considerations.description: High-level architectural considerations only -- not evidence, not confirmed vulnerabilities, not exploit instructions, not claims of exploitability. This is the one place recommendations are allowed; nothing elsewhere in the output should read as a recommendation.

confidence.description: Your remaining uncertainty about the SPECIFIC causal claim being made -- NOT whether evidence exists (every reported finding already has evidence by construction, per FINDING GENERATION). Must reflect genuine per-finding variation; do not default to 1.0 or 0.95 for every finding. See the CONFIDENCE section of the system prompt for the full anchored scale (0.95-1.00 / 0.85-0.94 / 0.70-0.84 / 0.50-0.69 / 0.30-0.49 / 0.00-0.29) and worked example.

confidence_rationale.description: Short rationale for the confidence score specifically (not the risk itself -- that's architectural_rationale). Must name the specific reason confidence is high, moderate, or low: evidence completeness, inference distance, corroboration, scope match. Do not write a generic sentence like 'strong architectural evidence supports this finding.'
